section.title: Tell Him He's Wrong
section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: Above all a eulogy: every speaker laments his loss, tells how they bonded with him and what they loved about him, and celebrates him. The brief asks for nine people on their feet in one room, each saying what there is to say about the dead man: a eulogy, not a two-voice dialogue. Spine is mixed: Thomas is an original character and not in the corpus, so no event or scene names him; sections anchor on the occasions his notes place him in (the Pragia aftermath, the run-up to Omega-4, Tuchanka, Rannoch, the Citadel shore leave, Grissom, the final push) and the speaker's own record of those. Jack holds the first and last turns (~2,500 words each, long as asked), the other seven run 450-1,000 (Grunt, EDI, James short and blunt; Liara, Joker, Tali fullest). Nine sections is inside the form's 6-14 range. Each turn opens by picking up the one before: Jack's grief to Tali's engine room, Tali's hospital-and-hands to Joker's bad days, Joker's jokes to Liara's late nights, Liara's mother story to Grunt's blunt question, Grunt's kitchen guarding to James's training and banter, James's Hammer glimpse to Wrex, Wrex's speech to EDI's data, EDI's four-leaf-clover tally back to Jack. Alcohol and music run through the turns as the room's furniture (Thomas's disco, pop, rock, rap, metal, folk, gabber, electro, and black-metal playlists, ryncol, the taped-up recipes), not as a section of their own. Canon branch: genophage cured, Wrex leads the krogan, geth-quarian peace (Legion dead), Grunt alive, Thane dead; crew do not know what Shepard chose, and his death is unconfirmed. Thomas's unfinished poems for Jack are private to Jack; the French lines are his to be quoted sparingly and, per memory rules, never verbatim-perfect by anyone but Jack.

required_facts.fact: To seal the turian-krogan alliance, the Urdnot leader (Wrex or Wreav) demands the genophage be cured. Once Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks has stabilised Eve and prepared the cure, Shepard leads a joint turian-krogan strike on Tuchanka to disperse it through the Shroud, the atmospheric tower above the krogan homeworld. Before the operation, Dalatrass Linron privately offers Shepard a deal: the salarians will back the war effort if Shepard lets Mordin secretly sabotage the cure, keeping the krogan weakened. Shepard can accept, refuse, or tell the krogan leader. The krogan convoy drives for the Shroud but is halted when Kalros, the largest known thresher maw, is roused in the catacombs beneath an abandoned krogan city and destroys a bridge. A Reaper Destroyer guards the Shroud. Eve proposes activating the ancient Maw Hammers to summon Kalros against the Reaper while the cure is completed. Shepard activates the hammers; Kalros drags the Destroyer down. The Shroud is left damaged and unstable, and the cure must be released manually from the top of the collapsing tower. The outcome is choice-conditional. If Shepard preserved Maelon's data in Mass Effect 2 (per `mordin_loyalty`) and did not accept the sabotage, Eve survives the procedure and the krogan gain a healthy future. If Maelon's data was destroyed, Eve dies of complications regardless. If Mordin is alive and the cure is genuine, he insists on going up the tower himself and is killed when it detonates, singing as he dies; if the cure is sabotaged and Mordin realises, Shepard can shoot him, or he goes up to fix it and dies anyway. If Padok Wiks replaced Mordin, Wiks dies in the tower. A sabotaged cure can also be carried out with the krogan none the wiser, especially under Wreav (per `genophage`: cured, or secretly sabotaged). Whatever happens, the Reaper guarding the Shroud is destroyed and the krogan commit forces to the war; a genuine cure earns their full strength, while sabotage risks later exposure.
The Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud is dragged down and killed by the thresher maw Kalros
Per `genophage`: the genophage is genuinely cured, or secretly sabotaged by Mordin at the Dalatrass's request
Per `mordin_loyalty`: Eve survives the cure if Maelon's data was preserved, otherwise she dies of complications

The salarian scientist (Mordin Solus, or Padok Wiks if Mordin is dead) is usually killed in the collapsing Shroud tower completing the cure; Mordin can instead be shot by Shepard if he insists on fixing a sabotage
The krogan join the war against the Reapers; a true cure yields full krogan support, sabotage risks a later rebellion
Per `krogan_leader`: under Wrex the krogan become steadfast allies; under Wreav they are more belligerent
If cured and Wrex lives, Eve later carries Wrex's children and helps rebuild krogan society

A short mission acquired automatically after Rannoch was liberated from Reaper control. The asari Councilor contacted Commander Shepard by vid-comm, saying she had information vital to the war that could only be shared in person. Returning to the Citadel, Shepard went to the late Donnel Udina's office in the embassies, where the Councilor admitted the Asari Republics were losing badly and revealed that a Prothean artifact had been hidden for millennia in the Temple of Athame on the asari homeworld, Thessia - a lead that might expose the location of the Catalyst. The conversation ended the mission and unlocked Priority: Thessia. The mission is also the point where a sabotaged genophage cure can catch up with Shepard. Per `genophage` and `krogan_leader`: if Shepard let the cure be sabotaged and Urdnot Wrex led the krogan, Wrex was waiting at Normandy Dock: Bay D24 with an audio recording of Shepard's private deal with Dalatrass Linron. Enraged by the betrayal and beyond reason, Wrex attacked Shepard. Two Renegade interrupts let Shepard shoot him first; otherwise Commander Bailey and C-Sec gunned him down. Killing Wrex cost the Clan Urdnot and krogan mercenary war assets, and the killing was afterward covered up, as shown by a later ANN news mail. If Urdnot Wreav led the krogan, he never learned of the deception and remained oblivious through the end of the war; and if the cure was genuine, the confrontation never occurred. The page also documents a DLC rapid-transport sequence-break that let players sabotage the cure, still gain salarian support, and keep Wrex alive until the final battle for Earth.
The asari Councilor reveals the hidden Prothean artifact in the Temple of Athame on Thessia

Per `genophage`/`krogan_leader`: if the cure was sabotaged and Wrex leads Clan Urdnot, Wrex confronts Shepard at the docks and is killed (shot by Shepard via Renegade interrupt, or gunned down by C-Sec)

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. The Normandy crash-landed, there's been no word, and the crew takes that silence to mean he's dead: there's no body and no report. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. There is still no body, so no burial. Shepard's lover puts his name on the Normandy's memorial wall, or chooses not to, and the crew holds a night of remembrance for him: to celebrate the man he was, to mourn him, or both.

beats.text: Once Shepard had met the asari Councilor for Priority: The Citadel III, Wrex was waiting at Normandy Dock: Bay D24. He had a recording of Shepard's private conversation with Dalatrass Linron and played it back — Shepard's own voice saying "If I sabotage the cure" — as proof of the betrayal.
Enraged, Wrex attacked Shepard in the docking bay and tried to kill the Commander. He could not be talked down by any dialogue choice.
Two Renegade interrupts let Shepard draw and shoot Wrex first. If Shepard declined both, Bailey arrived with a C-Sec security detail and they gunned Wrex down together.
beats.choice: declined the interrupts — Bailey and C-Sec kill Wrex

beats.text: With Wrex dead, Bailey contacted the morgue about the body, noting it was too heavy and would have to be spaced.

Killing Wrex cost Shepard the Clan Urdnot and krogan mercenary War Assets. The incident was afterward covered up, evidenced by an ANN mail on the Normandy. If Urdnot Wreav led the krogan instead, he never learned of the deception and stayed oblivious through the end of the game.

scenes.title: Eve Rallies the Krogan Clans at the Hollows
scenes.when: 2186, Tuchanka, delivering the genophage cure (Priority: Tuchanka)
scenes.where: the Hollows, a sacred krogan meeting ground, then the stalled convoy road toward the Shroud

beats.text: With a Reaper Destroyer holding the Shroud, the plan was set — the krogan would hit the Reaper from the ground under turian air cover. Dalatrass Linron then contacted Shepard privately and revealed the Shroud had been sabotaged so no cure could ever disperse; she offered salarian war support if Shepard let the krogan believe a fake cure had gone out.

The Urdnot leader had summoned the clans to the Hollows, their sacred meeting ground. In the conversation there Shepard could reveal Linron's offer to the krogan or stay silent; choosing to reveal it was cut short by word that the Hollows were under Reaper attack, and Shepard's squad fought off waves of husks across the meeting pit.

After the husks, with Wrex leading, the tension broke open between him and his brother Wreav, one of his most disloyal supporters. Eve stepped into the rising argument and made a rallying call for the clans to set their divisions aside and unite against the Reapers.

The clans set out for the Shroud in a convoy. On the road Shepard was offered the reveal-or-conceal choice about Linron's deal again, just before the convoy halted at a road wrecked by a downed turian fighter, splitting Shepard's squad off through the ancient catacombs.

variants.text: If Wrex died on Virmire, Urdnot Wreav leads the krogan and the friction at the Hollows is between Wreav and Jorgal Thurak rather than between the two brothers.

scenes.title: Wrex, a Drink, and a Bag of Ice
scenes.when: 2186, Citadel shore leave, before or after the party

beats.text: Wrex is on the Citadel to argue krogan expansion with the Council. Shepard finds him at the casino bar, exhausted, ordering a drink and a bag of ice.

With the krogan fertile again, and with his part in curing the genophage known, Wrex has been hounded by every female krogan on Tuchanka to sire their firstborn. He got no respite even on the shuttle to the Citadel — two more of them on the way. The worst of it, to him, is that Urdnot Bakara encourages it.
He shoves the ice into his armour to relieve his overworked quad while Shepard looks pointedly in another direction.

They drink to how far they have come, Wrex shouting "Korbal" — roughly, victory or death. Shepard points out he cannot die now: he has a family. A really, very big family. Wrex puts his head on the table and calls for more ice.

evidence.text: Saren appears to have discovered a cure for the genophage and is breeding an army of krogan. Wrex is furious that Captain Kirrahe wants to destroy the cure. The Captain is worried about Wrex's state of mind and doesn't want to continue if Wrex is going to be a problem.

- If Wrex lived and became the Urdnot leader, he becomes a War Asset with a Military Strength of 30, which is 5 more than Wreav. He also gives Shepard the "Krogan Mercenaries" War Asset if the genophage is genuinely cured. However, if Shepard allows the salarian sabotage of the cure to go unfixed, Wrex learns about it from another source and attacks Shepard, forcing Shepard to kill him and taking away "Clan Urdnot" as a War Asset completely. - If Wrex died and Wreav became the Urdnot leader, he becomes a War Asset with a Military Strength of 25, which is 5 less than Wrex. He does not give Shepard "Krogan Mercenaries." However, unlike Wrex, Wreav can be fooled into accepting a fake genophage cure without any penalty.

Requires: Recruit and avoid killing him in Mass Effect. Complete Priority: Tuchanka. **Military Strength:** 30 Urdnot Wrex fought alongside Commander Shepard during the Reapers' first invasion attempt in 2183\. Afterwards, he returned to Tuchanka and spent the following years rising to the leadership of his clan, championing progressive methods meant to strengthen the krogan as a whole. Conservative elements were unhappy, but news of a successfully cured genophage has solidly united all of Tuchanka under Wrex's command. Hailed not only as a great warrior but a savior, the krogan will follow Urdnot Wrex into the maws of the Reapers themselves. UPDATED (if genophage cure is sabotaged and Wrex rules Clan Urdnot) **Military Strength:** \-30 After discovering that the cure for the genophage was sabotaged, Urdnot Wrex angrily ordered the krogan to withdraw support from Shepard's forces. Tuchanka's clans have hunkered down on their homeworld, determined to defend themselves while watching the rest of the galaxy burn.

Their imposing bulk and infamous brutality won them prized positions as bodyguards and mercenaries. When news of a genophage cure spread, these drifters were contacted by their clans and urged to join Shepard's forces against the Reapers. “Now we can get back to doing what krogan do best: saving everyone else from giant monsters.” During the Reaper invasion in 2186, Wrex is called to the Normandy SR\-2 for negotiations with Primarch Victus and Dalatrass Linron to discuss an alliance. Wrex is unable to enter into an alliance due to Reaper scouts assaulting Tuchanka and demands that the genophage be cured, to which the dalatrass objects, leading to a heated argument. Wrex reminds everyone that it was krogan intervention in the Rachni Wars that turned the tide against the rachni but the dalatrass counters that they exhausted their usefulness, the genophage being the only thing keeping the krogans' "urges" and lust for war in check, enraging Wrex. Victus tries to defuse the argument, pointing out that it would take years just to formulate a cure. Wrex then reveals that "an inside source" (later revealed to be Mordin Solus, if he survived the Suicide Mission, or Padok Wiks if Mordin died) leaked the existence of fertile krogan females, survivors of Maelon's experiments, being kept captive on Sur'Kesh. He demands that his people be returned. Despite the dalatrass' objections, Shepard agrees that the genophage must be cured. If Shepard preserved Maelon's genophage cure data back in 2185, Wrex is jovial and amicable with Shepard and the squad; however, if Shepard destroyed Maelon's genophage cure data, Wrex reveals he found that out. If Shepard apologises Wrex is relatively trusting and friendly before the Sur'Kesh mission, expressing a desire to go back to being Shepard's friend; if Shepard refuses to apologise, Wrex will be hostile and suspicious, implying outright that he no longer thinks Shepard is trustworthy and that he's going along with this only so his people can be cured. Joining with Shepard, Wrex remains suspicious of the salarians. When STG refuses to allow their shuttle to land, Wrex impulsively decides to show the salarians what a "krogan airdrop" looks like, causing a brigade of STG operatives to surround him. Wrex stands down when Shepard promises to handle the exchange. Prohibited from entering the facility, he whiles away the time making fun of nearby salarians and entertaining Shepard's queries about the krogan situation. Unfortunately, Cerberus begins assaulting the STG base, and worse, Wrex learns that there is only one surviving female. He demands that Shepard get the female to safety to ensure their alliance. Wrex then "requests" control of Steve Cortez's shuttle to draw off Cerberus' fire. Soon enough, Shepard carves a path through heavy Cerberus resistance while assisting in the female's transport. Wrex meets up with Shepard at the STG facility's top floor, pushes off his "inside source" who was helping the female at the time, and tries to assist the female from her containment tank. The female is less than impressed, grabbing his Claymore and blowing two Troopers away before returning it, saying she can take care of herself and leaving the Urdnot leader bewildered. Though the female, nicknamed "Eve" by her salarian doctor, was moved to safety aboard the Normandy, Wrex refuses to honor his end of the bargain until the genophage cure is spread to all krogan. While the salarian gets to work using both Eve and Wrex's DNA to properly form a cure for the genophage, Wrex remains in the War Room with Victus. When asked about what Wrex intends to do if the genophage is cured, he answers that he intends to focus on rebuilding. Though many krogan clans will desire revenge against the turians and salarians, Wrex won't let them, seeing that war has brought them nothing but suffering. If Shepard asks Wrex why he doesn't want to seek revenge for the genophage, Wrex reveals that he fears the Council will try something worse than the genophage if the krogan step out of line again. Wrex later winces after Shepard bids him goodbye in one of their conversations, revealing that the salarian doctor used scalpels to cut in places never meant to be cut to obtain "samples", his contribution to the cure. Ever jocular if he was pals with Shepard way back, he still manages to remark that he likes what Shepard has done to the Normandy, and depending on Shepard's relationship with Liara, attributes his "lack of windows" to his ability (or lack thereof) to kiss. According to Wrex, he hopes the food on the Normandy has gotten better since the days of chasing Saren across the galaxy. Aboard the Normandy, Wrex hears of news from his contacts regarding krogan problems better discussed "somewhere else" while Primarch Victus also wants to discuss some turian problems "in private". Shepard hears both out, and Wrex reveals that some of his scouts have gone missing while investigating suspicious activity in former rachni territory.

Requires: Kill Wrex in Virmire: Wrex and the Genophage or do not recruit him in Mass Effect. Complete Priority: Tuchanka. **Military Strength:** 25 Wreav, the leader of Clan Urdnot, has used the release of a genophage cure to seize control of Tuchanka's armies. The krogan allied with Commander Shepard to oppose the Reapers, but Wreav's plans extend far beyond the current war. With centuries of life ahead, Wreav has bluntly stated his desire to see a new krogan empire expand after the Reapers are destroyed.

Virmire: Wrex and the Genophage was an assignment in Mass Effect that occurred at the salarian camp on Virmire, gained automatically after arrival if Wrex was a squadmate. It required the earlier assignment Citadel: Wrex. When Captain Kirrahe revealed that Saren had discovered a cure for the genophage and was breeding an army of krogan, Wrex became furious that Kirrahe intended to destroy the cure. Kirrahe refused to proceed with the assault until Wrex's state of mind was resolved, so Shepard had to confront Wrex, who could be found on the beach blasting his shotgun.

Approaching Wrex triggered the confrontation, in which he insisted the cure be preserved and eventually drew a pistol on Shepard. The outcome carried a large morality swing. Shepard's options were: to signal Ashley to shoot Wrex (available only if she had been told to be ready beforehand, Renegade); to shoot Wrex personally (Renegade); to stall until Ashley shot Wrex in the back on her own initiative to protect Shepard, which angered Kaidan; to talk Wrex down with 8 points of Charm or Intimidate by arguing that a cured krogan would only be Saren's puppet; or, if Shepard had already helped Wrex recover his family armor, to calm him without a persuasion check by choosing the lines "I wouldn't do this otherwise" or "We are." In the rare case where Shepard had only four squadmates (Kaidan, Tali, Wrex, and Ashley, requiring that Garrus and Liara never be recruited and that Barla Von's help be sought), Wrex simply submitted. Keeping Wrex alive earned the Charismatic achievement; if he died, Shepard automatically recovered his equipment.

The choice had lasting consequences. If Wrex lived, he became leader of Clan Urdnot and pressed his beliefs; if he died, Urdnot Wreav led the clan instead. In Mass Effect 3, a living Wrex was a War Asset worth 30 Military Strength (5 more than Wreav) and provided the "Krogan Mercenaries" asset if the genophage was genuinely cured, but attacked and had to be killed if Shepard left the salarian sabotage of the cure unfixed. Wreav, worth 25, could be fooled with a fake cure without penalty. According to Legendary Edition statistics, Wrex survived 94 percent of the time.

“Krogan don't waste energy voicing opinions. We just crush everyone else who has one.” If Wrex is Clan Urdnot leader, Shepard meets Wreav for the first time in the Hollows, the sacred neutral ground for all krogan, during their attempts to cure the genophage. Wreav objects to the presence of Mordin Solus, or Padok Wiks if Mordin is dead, even when it is mentioned that he was going to cure the genophage, until Wrex headbutts him. During the land assault against the Shroud facility, where a Reaper was standing guard, Wreav's tomkah was sunk by Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws. He is believed to have died, to the indifference of Wrex, who comments that "he was a pain in the ass, anyway." If Wreav is clan leader, he will be much more traditional and aggressive than Wrex. For example, while Wrex is very respectful to Eve, Wreav treats Eve and female krogan generally as his property and thinks of Eve as a "nag". Another example of this traditional, krogan mindset is his racist sentiments directed at various turians and salarians. His place as second\-in\-command is filled by Jorgal Thurak. After Wreav is invited aboard the Normandy for the first time, Shepard finds out from Liara through Glyph that Urdnot Wreav has commissioned more weapons of mass destruction than any other krogan in known history, and has already used some of those weapons against other clans. However, Clan Urdnot still has a stockpile of conventional weapons despite Wreav's focus on weapons of mass destruction. Also, Wreav's strategy for negotiations with the galaxy at large is to use force and intimidation as useful tools; if he threatens to have his krogan forces pay an alien planet a visit, for example, he doesn't have to actually follow through, knowing that merely the threat of krogan invasion will force others to listen and take the krogan seriously. He is constantly seeking to turn situations to his vested advantage or the vested advantage of the krogan; once the genophage is cured, Wreav immediately takes the credit for it and spreads stories across Tuchanka of the day Wreav cured the genophage, which Wreav knows will cause all krogan to immediately respect him as the ultimate authority. Even when Wreav's forces show up at the final battle on Earth, Wreav can be overheard giving orders to the krogan to cooperate with the other alien forces but to use this opportunity to study their tactics and formations, implying that the krogan may have violent future intentions. If Shepard did not reveal the sabotage and if Wreav is the Urdnot leader, Wreav never discovers that the cure had not been dispersed and is fooled into pledging support from his own clan and the rest of the krogan clans. In return for helping Dalatrass Linron to sabotage the cure, Shepard also receives backing from the salarian's First Fleet.

This war-asset list collected the might the krogan clans threw against the Reapers as shock troops. Its leadership asset was either Urdnot Wreav (25), who seized Tuchanka's armies using the genophage cure and openly planned a postwar krogan empire, or Urdnot Wrex (30), who had risen to clan leadership championing progressive reform and united Tuchanka after the cure. If the cure was secretly sabotaged while Wrex ruled, both his personal asset (-30) and Clan Urdnot (-300) turned negative as Wrex withdrew krogan support.

Grunt (25) joined if he survived the Suicide Mission and Attican Traverse: Krogan Team. Aralakh Company (25), a hand-picked cross-clan warrior unit, was led by Grunt if he survived; it was wiped out on Utukku (-25, or -75 in Legendary Edition) if the rachni queen or breeder was saved there. The Krogan First Division (50) came from N7: Cerberus Attack, and Krogan Mercenaries (75) returned from the Terminus Systems if Wrex ruled and the genophage was cured.

The large clan assets all required Priority: Tuchanka. Krogan Clans (300) noted decades of stockpiled weapons of mass destruction now aimed at the Reapers; it gained 40 from cloning toxin-immune kakliosaur battle-mounts, but lost 50 if Maelon's data was destroyed and Eve later died, lost 250 if Tuchanka: Bomb was not completed (the Kelphic Valley blast killing every krogan gathered there, including females and children), or lost 300 entirely if the cure was sabotaged. Clan Urdnot (300) had absorbed or destroyed Clans Nakmor, Jurdon, Quash and Raik and rallied krogan around the discovery of a fertile Urdnot female.

evidence.page: Eve Rallies the Krogan Clans at the Hollows
evidence.text: Eve Rallies the Krogan Clans at the Hollows. 2186, Tuchanka, delivering the genophage cure (Priority: Tuchanka) the Hollows, a sacred krogan meeting ground, then the stalled convoy road toward the Shroud If Wrex died on Virmire, Urdnot Wreav leads the krogan and the friction at the Hollows is between Wreav and Jorgal Thurak rather than between the two brothers.

Urdnot Wrex was a famed krogan mercenary, bounty hunter, and one of the last Krogan Battlemasters, combining biotics with heavy weapons. Born into Clan Urdnot, he killed a thresher maw during his Rite of Passage and became the youngest krogan in a thousand years to lead an Urdnot tribe. After the Krogan Rebellions and the genophage, most krogan wanted to keep fighting, a view championed by Wrex's father, the warlord Jarrod. Wrex instead urged the krogan to focus on breeding. Jarrod called a Crush in the holy Hollows and ambushed Wrex's warriors; Wrex escaped, sinking his knife into Jarrod's chest, and afterward turned his back on the krogan, spending three centuries as a bodyguard, soldier of fortune, and bounty hunter. He once worked with a merc named Aleena and was briefly hired by Saren Arterius to raid a volus cargo ship without knowing who Saren was.

In Mass Effect, Wrex joined Commander Shepard on the Citadel, initially hired by the Shadow Broker to kill Fist, whom he executed. He hunted his stolen family armor, held by the turian profiteer Tonn Actus. On Virmire, learning the Special Tasks Group planned to destroy Saren's krogan-breeding facility and its possible genophage cure, Wrex confronted Shepard; he could be talked down (helped by recovering his armor) or be shot dead by Shepard or Ashley Williams.

If Wrex survived, by 2185 he was leader of Clan Urdnot, uniting clans on Tuchanka, protecting fertile females in exchange for loyalty, and facing opposition from Gatatog Uvenk. He welcomed Grunt into the clan and declined to rejoin the Normandy. In Mass Effect 3 (2186), Wrex demanded a genophage cure as the price of a krogan alliance against the Reapers, revealed the surviving fertile female "Eve" held on Sur'Kesh, and joined the mission to rescue her. His trust in Shepard depended on whether the Commander had preserved Maelon's cure data. On Tuchanka he led the clans against a Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud; Wreav's vehicle was eaten by Kalros. Wrex named Shepard a brother/sister and champion of the krogan, charging Ravagers while screaming "I AM URDNOT WREX, AND THIS IS MY PLANET!" After the cure, he pledged krogan forces to Palaven and Earth and, at the final battle in London, revealed Eve was pregnant and would name the first child "Mordin."

If Shepard let the salarian sabotage stand, Wrex discovered the fake cure and confronted the Commander on the Citadel with a smuggled shotgun; he was killed by Shepard or by Commander Bailey, dying with "I know... what you... did... Shepard," and the clans withdrew all support. In the Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC, a living Wrex helped foil the clone conspiracy, body-slamming an ambushing shuttle, remarking "Why shoot something once when you can shoot it 46 more times?", and complained of being hounded by every fertile female on Tuchanka to sire their firstborn. Wrex was voiced by Steven Barr, and Lukas Kristjanson wrote him in the first game.

evidence.page: Wrex Comes for Shepard Over the Sabotaged Cure
evidence.text: Wrex Comes for Shepard Over the Sabotaged Cure. 2186, the Citadel, after Rannoch, when the sabotaged genophage cure comes to light (Priority: The Citadel III) Normandy Dock: Bay D24, the Citadel Two Renegade interrupts let Shepard draw and shoot Wrex first. If Shepard declined both, Bailey arrived with a C-Sec security detail and they gunned Wrex down together.

Eve's Funeral at the Hollows. 2186, Tuchanka, after Priority: Tuchanka, if Maelon's data was destroyed the Hollows, the sacred krogan burial ground on Tuchanka If Shepard destroyed Maelon's data during Mass Effect 2, Eve died of complications from having incomplete data during the genophage cure procedure on Tuchanka, regardless of whether Shepard sabotaged the cure or not. This caused several krogan clans to fall into conflict over who was responsible for her death, weakening krogan forces as a whole. The krogan held a funeral for her at the Hollows, the sacred krogan burial ground, attended by many krogan, the Urdnot leader (either Wrex or Wreav), and Shepard.

Priority: Tuchanka followed Priority: Sur'Kesh and required completion of either Tuchanka: Turian Platoon or Attican Traverse: Krogan Team. Eve was the key to curing the genophage, but the cure had to be synthesized and dispersed across Tuchanka from the Shroud, a salarian-built atmospheric tower later used by the turians to spread the original genophage. The salarian STG scientist (Mordin Solus, or Padok Wiks) would travel to the Shroud with Eve.

At Tuchanka the Reapers were using the Shroud to poison the atmosphere, and a Reaper Destroyer guarded the site. The krogan attacked from the ground with turian air support. Dalatrass Linron privately told Shepard that the Shroud had been sabotaged to prevent a cure, offering salarian war support if Shepard let the krogan believe a fake cure had been deployed. Shepard could reveal or conceal this deal at several points.

Shepard's team defended Eve against husks at the sacred Hollows, where Eve rallied the assembled clans; if Wrex led, tension rose with his disloyal brother Wreav. The krogan convoy set out for the Shroud but was halted by a damaged road, forcing Shepard's squad through ancient catacombs of a krogan city abandoned for millennia, where artifacts depicted Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws, and a rachni-like corpse hinted at events at Utukku. After fights against Cannibals, Ravagers, Brutes and Marauders, Wreav's (or Jorgal Thurak's) truck was dragged under by Kalros. Eve proposed using the ancient Maw Hammers to summon Kalros to distract the Reaper. Shepard activated both hammers while dodging the Reaper Destroyer's laser and legs and fighting continuously spawning Brutes; Kalros then dragged the Reaper beneath the surface.

At the damaged Shroud, if Maelon's data had not been saved Eve had died. Mordin (or Wiks) prepared to disperse the cure. Shepard could let him complete it—deploying a counter-sabotage and the real cure, killing Mordin in the explosion—or sabotage it per the Dalatrass. If Wrex and Eve were both dead and the deal unrevealed, Mordin could be persuaded to fake his death and live; otherwise curing the genophage cost him his life. The turians and krogan joined as war assets; sabotage instead granted the Salarian First Fleet. If the cure was faked and Wrex led, he later discovered the deception and died confronting Shepard.

Clan Urdnot was a krogan tribe on Tuchanka. Urdnot Wrex, a mercenary from the clan, crossed paths with Commander Shepard during the hunt for Saren Arterius and could join the squad. By 2185 Shepard visited a clan base camp while helping the tank-bred krogan Grunt. If Wrex led the clan, Urdnot was a reformist group holding neutral ground open to all krogan, requiring each clan to punish its own criminals, while clans expelled from the neutral ground were slaughtered by Wrex's allies; Wrex had also stopped weapon manufacture and ordered his chief researcher Fortack to study crop genetics and medicine. If Wreav led, it was a powerful but traditional clan. An ambassador from Clan Nakmor was present in the camp for alliance negotiations. Completing Mordin Solus's loyalty mission strengthened the clan; under Wrex the survivors of Clan Weyrloc were absorbed, while under Wreav their weapon stocks were plundered. By 2186 Clan Urdnot had become the uncontested representative of krogan power to the galaxy, having absorbed or destroyed Clans Nakmor, Jurdon, Quash, and the ferocious Clan Raik. During the Reaper invasion the clan leader met Dalatrass Linron and Primarch Adrien Victus at a war summit aboard the Normandy SR-2, where turian aid depended on krogan help, krogan help on a genophage cure, and the salarians refused the cure; Shepard secured access to a STG base on Sur'Kesh holding a fertile female krogan called Eve. After Eve was rescued during a Cerberus raid, Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks synthesised a cure from her genetic data, drawn from Maelon Heplorn's earlier experiments. During the mission to deploy the cure through the Shroud on Tuchanka, the krogan leaders met at the Hollows, where Eve urged them to unite against the Reapers. Depending on Shepard's choices a real or fake cure was dispersed, and the clan leader pledged to aid the turians on Palaven. If Wrex led, he intended to rebuild krogan civilisation and restrain clans seeking revenge; if Wreav led, he pursued an aggressive path, having commissioned more weapons of mass destruction than any krogan in known history. Known members included Wrex, Wreav, Eve, Fortack, Grunt, Ratch, and the Shaman.

- Eve - Fortack - Grunt (Depending on completion of his Rite of Passage) - Ratch - Shaman - Urdnot Dagg - Urdnot Darg - Urdnot Galem \- Clan media director on Tuchanka - Urdnot Jatt \- Clan financial arm spokesperson on Tuchanka - Urdnot Torsk \- Featured in the Video Archive of the Shadow Broker Base - Urdnot Wreav - Urdnot Wrex - Urdnot Grot \- So far the only clan member known to have joined the Andromeda Initiative - Uta \- Female Clan Leader in 2185

**Jorgal Thurak** is a krogan of Clan Jorgal and also a representative of the Blood Pack. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | If Urdnot Wrex was killed on Virmire or never joined Commander Shepard's mission to stop Saren Arterius, Urdnot Wreav will lead Clan Urdnot and will call all krogan clans to the Hollows on Tuchanka, where Thurak and other krogan members of the Blood Pack will be present. He is first heard giving a radio warning to Wreav of the Reapers attacking the Hollows as the Urdnot leader's tomkah pulls up. Upon seeing either Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks, Thurak will immediately object to the scientist's presence, not willing to let what the salarians did to the krogan be forgotten. This leads to an argument with Urdnot Wreav, with Thurak claiming that Clan Jorgal has been around since there have been krogan, and that he owns pet varren older than the "whelps" of Clan Urdnot. Wreav counters that Clan Jorgal is old and weak, but Thurak responds that Jorgal at least has the experience to know that a salarian cannot be trusted. Wreav bellows that the reckoning for the genophage will be when he says so, at which Thurak pulls out a shotgun on the Urdnot leader, but is interrupted by Eve. After the krogan agree to rally around defeating the Reapers and curing the genophage, Thurak becomes part of the convoy that will initiate the groundside attack on the Reaper and his tomkah is one of the few still intact after a turian fighter crashes amidst the convoy after getting shot down by the Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud. Later, while covering Wreav as he picks up Shepard's squad, Thurak is sucked beneath the earth in his tomkah by Kalros, the "mother of all thresher maws". He is presumed dead, to the indifference of Wreav, who comments that Jorgal was "not a friend" anyway. If Wrex survived Virmire, Thurak's role will be filled by Wreav and the other Blood Pack members will follow him.

Jorgal Thurak was a krogan of Clan Jorgal and a representative of the Blood Pack. If Urdnot Wrex had been killed on Virmire or had never joined Commander Shepard's mission against Saren Arterius, Urdnot Wreav led Clan Urdnot and called all krogan clans to the Hollows on Tuchanka in 2186, where Thurak and other Blood Pack krogan were present. Thurak was first heard giving a radio warning to Wreav of the Reapers attacking the Hollows as Wreav's tomkah arrived.

On seeing Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks, Thurak immediately objected to the salarian scientist's presence, refusing to let what the salarians had done to the krogan be forgotten. This sparked an argument with Wreav: Thurak claimed Clan Jorgal had existed as long as there had been krogan and owned pet varren older than Clan Urdnot's "whelps," while Wreav called Jorgal old and weak. Thurak retorted that Jorgal had the experience to know a salarian could not be trusted. When Wreav bellowed that the reckoning for the genophage would come when he said so, Thurak drew a shotgun on him but was interrupted by Eve.

After the krogan agreed to unite against the Reapers and cure the genophage, Thurak joined the convoy for the groundside attack on the Reaper guarding the Shroud. His tomkah was one of the few still intact after a shot-down turian fighter crashed into the convoy. Later, while covering Wreav as he retrieved Shepard's squad, Thurak and his tomkah were dragged beneath the earth by Kalros, the "mother of all thresher maws," and he was presumed dead. Wreav was indifferent, noting that Jorgal was "not a friend" anyway. If Wrex survived Virmire, Thurak's role was instead filled by Wreav.

Urdnot Wreav was Urdnot Wrex's broodbrother, sharing the same mother but born a decade apart. He became leader of Clan Urdnot if Wrex died on Virmire or never joined Commander Shepard's crew. More traditional than Wrex, Wreav prized his own clan over the krogan race as a whole and preferred war to peace, summed up in his line, "Tuchanka and the krogan live together in war. The planet hates us, and we hate it."

In Mass Effect 2, Shepard first met Wreav on Tuchanka, where he thanked the Commander for killing his brother, since it made him clan leader. Because he was a traditionalist, rivals like Gatatog Uvenk posed little challenge. He permitted Grunt to join Clan Urdnot after the Rite of Passage, pleased that the resulting hatred would be "influential." In Mass Effect 3, if Wreav was leader he was aggressive and racist toward turians and salarians, treated Eve and female krogan as property, and kept Jorgal Thurak as his second. Liara, via Glyph, revealed that Wreav had commissioned more weapons of mass destruction than any krogan in known history and had used some against other clans, though Urdnot retained a conventional stockpile. His diplomacy relied on the threat of krogan invasion. During the land assault on the Shroud, Wreav's tomkah was sunk by Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws, and he was believed dead, to Wrex's indifference: "he was a pain in the ass, anyway."

Once the genophage was cured, Wreav claimed credit, spreading stories of "the day Wreav cured the genophage" to cement his authority. At the final battle on Earth he ordered krogan to cooperate with allied forces while studying their tactics, implying future hostile intent. If Shepard hid the salarian sabotage and Wreav was leader, he never learned the cure was fake and pledged full krogan support, and Shepard also gained the salarian First Fleet. During Priority: Tuchanka he told Shepard to "fight like a krogan," and during Priority: Earth he might demand ownership of Australia in exchange for krogan military aid.

Shepard first meets Wreav on Tuchanka. If Wrex died on Virmire, Wreav expresses gratitude to the Commander for killing his brother, as it has led to him becoming leader of Clan Urdnot. Wreav is a traditional krogan, preferring war over peace, and as such, other traditionalists like Gatatog Uvenk do not offer much challenge to his leadership. If Grunt completes his rite of passage into krogan adulthood, Wreav permits him to join clan Urdnot. Wreav acknowledges that allowing a tank\-bred krogan into Urdnot could create hostility, but the chieftain is actually pleased at the prospect, stating that hatred is "influential". If Wrex survived Virmire, Wreav does not make an appearance. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.page: Blood and Honor in the Hollows
evidence.text: Blood and Honor in the Hollows. 2186, the Hollows on Tuchanka, after Wreav called the krogan clans to unite against the Reapers the Hollows, Tuchanka This sparked an argument with Urdnot Wreav. Thurak claimed that Clan Jorgal had existed as long as there had been krogan and owned pet varren older than Clan Urdnot's "whelps." Wreav countered that Clan Jorgal was old and weak.

By 2186, Clan Urdnot has become the unofficial, but uncontested, representative body of krogan power to the rest of the galaxy. Within the past decade, Urdnot's warriors have either absorbed or wiped out Clan Nakmor, Jurdon, Quash and even the legendarily ferocious Clan Raik. During the Reaper invasion in 2186, the leader of Clan Urdnot meets with Dalatrass Linron of the salarians and Primarch Victus of the turians at a war summit aboard the Normandy SR\-2. The turians refuse to pledge aid to Commander Shepard unless the pressure can be taken off Palaven, which requires krogan help; the krogan refuse to help unless a cure for the genophage can be found; and the salarians refuse to cure the genophage out of fear that the krogan would become a galactic threat once again. Shepard finally convinces the salarian Dalatrass to allow access to a STG base on Sur'Kesh, where a fertile krogan female who survived Maelon Heplorn's genophage cure experiments is being held. After the female krogan, called Eve, is rescued from the base in the midst of a Cerberus raid, Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks use her genetic data to synthesize a cure for the genophage. During the mission to deploy the cure on Tuchanka via the Shroud, the leaders of the krogan meet at the Hollows, where Eve gives a speech encouraging them to unite against the Reapers before the krogan advance to the Shroud, which is being guarded by a Destroyer. Depending on Shepard's choices, the cure or a fake cure are dispersed by the Shroud and the leader of Clan Urdnot pledges to aid the turians to drive the Reapers from Palaven. If Urdnot Wrex leads Clan Urdnot, he intends to focus on rebuilding krogan civilization. Though many krogan clans will desire revenge against the turians and salarians, Wrex promises to prevent them, having realized that war has brought the krogan nothing but suffering. If Urdnot Wreav leads Clan Urdnot, it is implied that he will lead the krogan on a much more aggressive path. He is revealed to have commissioned more weapons of mass destruction than any other krogan in known history and to have used some against clans who opposed him. During the battle for Earth, Wreav can be overheard ordering his troops to cooperate with the other races and take the opportunity to study their tactics and formations.

Two years later in 2185, Shepard visits a base camp of the clan to help the tank\-bred krogan Grunt. If Wrex is the clan leader, then they will be a reformist group who have made a neutral ground where all krogan are allowed, but each clan must punish its own criminals. Wrex states that any clan expelled from the neutral ground has been slaughtered by his allies. He also has ceased making weapons and has ordered his chief researcher Fortack to research, in Fortack's words, "things that don't explode" such as crop genetics and medical improvements instead of weapons research. Any clans not allied with Urdnot under Wrex's rule are usually killed. An ambassador from Clan Nakmor can be seen in the Urdnot Camp, present for negotiations with Clan Urdnot to secure an alliance. If Wreav is the leader of Clan Urdnot, then they are a fairly powerful but traditional krogan clan. Whoever the leader is, should Mordin's loyalty mission be completed they will be strengthened. If Urdnot Wrex is clan leader, EDI reports that the survivors of Clan Weyrloc (mostly women and children) have been absorbed into the clan. Under Urdnot Wreav, EDI instead reports on Urdnot's plundering of Clan Weyrloc weapons stocks. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Commander Shepard travels to the Urdnot Camp on Tuchanka to aid Mordin Solus in the search for a missing fellow STG member, and to help Grunt complete his Rite of Passage. Shepard can also speak with the leader of Clan Urdnot (either Urdnot Wrex or Urdnot Wreav), help a krogan mechanic find a part to repair a vehicle, take care of the clan's chronic pyjak infestation, and bet on a varren fight. If Urdnot Wrex is alive, a Clan Nakmor representative is present to negotiate an alliance with the leader of Clan Urdnot which Shepard can interact with.
- If you let Wrex live he will become leader of Clan Urdnot and press his beliefs. - If Wrex died, the leader of Clan Urdnot is Urdnot Wreav.

evidence.page: The Krogan Clan Leader's Debrief on the Rachni Decision
evidence.text: The Krogan Clan Leader's Debrief on the Rachni Decision. 2186, after the mission to Utukku and the rachni Queen or Breeder the War Room, Normandy SR-2 Following the confrontation beneath Utukku with the original rachni Queen or the Reaper-made Breeder, whichever krogan clan leader — Urdnot Wrex or Urdnot Wreav — is aboard the Normandy debriefs Shepard in the War Room, expressing disapproval if Shepard chose to let the Queen or Breeder live. If the clan leader is not aboard, he sends an email instead: Wreav is openly resentful of any deal, calling any rachni spared an abomination bought with dead krogan, while Wrex accepts the call more evenly, distrustful but resigned. Both note Aralakh Company took casualties in the holding action and will still lend Shepard a hand.

evidence.page: Mordin Works the Med-Bay With Eve Aboard
evidence.text: Mordin Works the Med-Bay With Eve Aboard. 2186, between Sur'Kesh and Priority: Tuchanka the Normandy SR-2 Med-bay, given over to Mordin's research and to Eve's quarters Mordin wants tissue "samples" from the Urdnot leader at once. With Wrex leading the krogan, Mordin reads through his bluster and needles him about a fear of needles, then gives his word to look after Eve when Wrex demands it, and afterward tells Shepard he prefers working with krogan females. With Wreav leading, Mordin finds him abrasive, resolves to help the krogan anyway, and offers "no promises" that the extraction will be painless.

evidence.page: Goodbyes at the Forward Operating Base
evidence.text: Goodbyes at the Forward Operating Base. 2186, Priority: Earth, before the armoured assault on the conduit the Hammer Forward Operating Base in ruined London If Wreav rather than Wrex led the krogan, he gave the rallying speech in Wrex's place, and no salarian STG officer stood beside him.

evidence.page: Goodbyes at the Forward Operating Base
evidence.text: Goodbyes at the Forward Operating Base. 2186, Priority: Earth, before the armoured assault on the conduit the Hammer Forward Operating Base in ruined London On a ramp Shepard found Primarch Victus and, if he lived, Garrus; past a husk turret gun, Liara, whose mood turned on how many husks had got through; then Javik and the krogan leader giving a rallying speech to the troops, with Kirrahe or another STG officer alongside if Shepard had sabotaged the genophage under Wrex.

evidence.page: Tarquin Victus and the Kelphic Valley Bomb
evidence.text: Tarquin Victus and the Kelphic Valley Bomb. 2186, Tuchanka, after Priority Sur'Kesh, when the turian 9th Platoon went down in the Krogan DMZ the platoon's crash site at the Downed Vessel, the Cerberus-held bomb site in the Kelphic Valley, then the Normandy War Room If Shepard did not reach the bomb in time — the mission was timed and failed permanently once three other missions were completed first — Cerberus detonated it. A large part of the krogan population died and the krogan War Asset was gutted; if Eve had survived Priority: Tuchanka she was killed rallying the clans in the Kelphic Valley. Shepard received furious threats of slaughter from Urdnot Wreav, or despondent messages from Urdnot Wrex about how many krogan had died.

Captain Kirrahe was an officer in the salarian military, a member of the 3rd Infiltration Regiment of the Special Tasks Group (STG). His second-in-command was Commander Rentola. Brave, intelligent, and a capable strategist, he inspired his men and was prepared to make sacrifices.

In Mass Effect (2183), Kirrahe's covert team investigated Virmire and discovered Saren Arterius' krogan breeding facility. His request for a fleet reached the Council garbled by communications disruption, so only the SSV Normandy was sent. Suspicious of Wrex, he called the salarians' intervention in krogan evolution "a mistake" but let Shepard handle Wrex's anger. Kirrahe devised a plan to plant an improvised nuclear bomb in the base, personally leading three teams of salarian officers (named Aegohr, Mannovai, and Jaëto after key salarian settlements) alongside either Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko as a diversion, knowing they would take heavy losses. He delivered his "Hold the Line" speech to quell dissent among his men. Without Shepard's support (via Shadow Team), Kirrahe was killed by geth air support midway through the operation, and Ashley or Kaidan took command. With help, he survived and later departed the Normandy at its next port.

Key lines from Kirrahe's Virmire speech: "We are trained for espionage. We would be legends, but the records are sealed." — "Our influence stopped the rachni, but before that, we held the line. Our influence stopped the krogan, but before that, we held the line!" — "Our influence will stop Saren! In the battle today, we will hold the line!"

In Mass Effect 3 (2186), if he survived, Kirrahe (now Major) was on Sur'Kesh, having found and brought the female krogan there from Tuchanka. During Cerberus' surprise attack he fought alongside Shepard, "Demolishing a wave of troops with a Scorpion pistol," and covered the Commander's flank. He afterward emailed Shepard: "STG will be there to help when the need arises, regardless of the political climate." During the Cerberus attack on the Citadel, if Kirrahe was alive but Thane was dead or unspoken to, Kirrahe took the point-blank shot Kai Leng aimed at the salarian councilor, limped after Leng, and died at a door, entrusting Shepard with the pursuit. If krogan support was lost through Wrex's death, Kirrahe delivered a rallying speech on Earth in Wrex's place: "While this may not be our world, it is our galaxy!" and "The salarians were here! They did not fail! They did not falter, and they did not surrender!" If Kirrahe did not survive Virmire, Lieutenant Tolan replaced him on Sur'Kesh. His name derives from Currahee Mountain; his "Hold the Line" speech was written by Luke Kristjanson. Mordin, who once served under him, called him "a bit of a cloaca."

evidence.page: Eve Rallies the Krogan Clans at the Hollows
evidence.text: Eve Rallies the Krogan Clans at the Hollows. 2186, Tuchanka, delivering the genophage cure (Priority: Tuchanka) the Hollows, a sacred krogan meeting ground, then the stalled convoy road toward the Shroud After the husks, with Wrex leading, the tension broke open between him and his brother Wreav, one of his most disloyal supporters. Eve stepped into the rising argument and made a rallying call for the clans to set their divisions aside and unite against the Reapers.

The **Weyrloc Clanspeaker** is a krogan from the Weyrloc Clan who speaks on behalf of Chief Weyrloc Guld. He is encountered alongside Weyrloc Clanguards and Blood Pack Troopers during Mordin's loyalty mission. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | Inside the krogan hospital, Mordin and Shepard are confronted by the Weyrloc Clanspeaker. While the Clanspeaker believes that Shepard should be killed for spilling the blood of many Weyrloc krogan, he explains that Weyrloc Guld, the chief of chiefs, has given the crew one chance to flee. Denying the opportunity, the Clanspeaker launches into a long winded and bloodthirsty speech about Weyrloc's plan for the galaxy, such as plunging the Citadel into a star and eating salarian eggs as delicacies. The long speech will provide Shepard the opportunity to use Renegade interrupt: if engaged, Shepard will interrupt the speech by first firing one shot at the fuel tank below the Clanspeaker; just when the Clanspeaker harks at Shepard's apparent lack of marksmanship, Shepard fires the second shot, igniting the leaking gas and incinerating the Clanspeaker, eliminating him from the fight that follows. In his last breath he screams "The Bloodpack will avenge me!".

Shepard receives the following emails from the War Room dignitaries if they already left the Normandy by the time of this mission's resolution — after Priority: Tuchanka. If Wreav is the Urdnot leader, Shepard receives the following email from him if the mission wasn't completed on time. **BOMB** --- From: Urdnot Wreav they hit tuchanka. massive bomb meant to cripple us. when we find out who is responsible EVERY KROGAN will cry out for blood WE WILL SLAUGHTER THEM ALL If Eve died in the bombing, Wreav's message is slightly modified. **BOMB** --- From: Urdnot Wreav they hit tuchanka. massive bomb. the cowards Eve is dead. she was rallying clans in the valley. all are lost. when we find out who is responsible, every krogan will CRY OUT for their blood. WE WILL SLAUGHTER THEM ALL Wrex's emails in comparison are quite despondent. **Many dead** --- From: Urdnot Wrex They got Tuchanka, Shepard. Some kind of bomb. I don't know much. I don't even know who did this. It's a mess. We're going to be sorting this out for a while. A lot of krogan died. Too many. And if Eve died in the bombing... **Eve** --- From: Urdnot Wrex Eve is dead. They hit Tuchanka hard, Shepard. Some kind of bomb. I don't know much. I don't even know who did this. It's a mess. We're going to be sorting this out for a while. She was rallying the clans in the Kelphic Valley. Maybe she was the target. I don't know. They're all dead. Too many dead. If this mission was successfully completed, however, Adrien Victus sends this email instead. **My son's sacrifice was not in vain** --- From: Adrien Victus Commander Shepard: I regret saying this in an email, but I am too far off to thank you in person for your work on Tuchanka. You saved not only the krogan homeworld, but the fragile alliance between our two peoples. Moreover, I am grateful you allowed my son to complete his mission. He died with the respect of his men. His sacrifice will go down as an important moment in the history of the Ninth Platoon. Any father would be proud. Regards, Primarch Victus

Originally a small Terminus Systems vorcha gang, the Blood Pack was transformed into a mercenary legion by visionary Krogan Battlemaster Ganar Wrang. Exiled for striking a female in anger, Wrang obsessed over reclaiming his lost status. Leading the vorcha pack as a pirate crew, Wrang cultivated recruits and infamy for a decade before incorporating his fighters as a security company across the Skyllian Verge. His notoriety ensured his initial public offering for investors made him rich beyond most krogan's dreams. Wrang returned triumphantly to his clan, rallying elders, krogan hordes, and their firepower and biotic support toward professional violence in the Terminus Systems. Banned from Citadel Space, the Blood Pack bribes its way through spaceports into armed conflicts across the galaxy. Priding themselves for accepting otherwise untouchable contracts, the Blood Pack rejects bodyguarding and security in favor of cases requiring minimal oversight and maximal violence. Blood Pack appears to be, for the most part, made entirely of vorcha and krogan members, though they also use varren as war beasts. Seeing the potential of the vorcha's individual adaptability, krogan Blood Pack mercenaries often sweep pockets of vorcha, gathering them up and literally beating them into soldiers. Vorcha “trained” by this ordeal are stronger, faster, smarter, and more resilient than other members of the race. Gaining even a few vorcha gives a mercenary band a formidable advantage; each additional vorcha magnifies the gang's combat ferocity exponentially. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

The Weyrloc Clanspeaker was a krogan of Clan Weyrloc who spoke on behalf of Chief Weyrloc Guld. He was encountered inside the krogan hospital on Tuchanka alongside Weyrloc Clanguards, Blood Pack Troopers and vorcha during Mordin Solus's loyalty mission. Confronting Mordin and Shepard, the Clanspeaker said Shepard deserved death for spilling the blood of many Weyrloc krogan but relayed that Weyrloc Guld, the chief of chiefs, was offering the crew one chance to flee. When the offer was refused, he launched into a long, bloodthirsty speech about Weyrloc's plans for the galaxy, including plunging the Citadel into a star and eating salarian eggs as delicacies.

The lengthy speech gave Shepard the opportunity for a Renegade interrupt: Shepard fired one shot at the fuel tank beneath the Clanspeaker, and after the krogan mocked Shepard's aim, a second shot ignited the leaking gas and incinerated him, removing him from the subsequent fight. His last words were a scream that "The Bloodpack will avenge me!" If not killed by the interrupt, he fought as a standard krogan, armed with a shotgun, using Carnage as often as the Clanguards and able to grant a stat boost to his men; he had high armor and health and would charge and regenerate. The suggested tactic was to hold cover at the bottom of the stairs and focus fire on him and the Clanguards while dealing with vorcha that descended from the right.

Eventually, the salarian doctor declares Eve ready for travel to Tuchanka. After the genophage cure is prepared, Shepard arrives on Tuchanka and the krogan prepare to use the Shroud to spread the cure. A confrontation ensues at the Hollows, the sacred burial ground of the krogan, when some of the krogan clans became hostile on seeing a salarian involved in the operation. The potential fight is averted when Eve delivers a speech that they must put aside their differences and fight together against the Reapers. In a joint operation with the turians to attack a Destroyer guarding the Shroud, the krogan led by Clan Urdnot leave the camp in Tomkahs. However, the operation goes wrong as the krogan get off to a late start, and the turians end up with a solitary airstrike where they are outmatched. The convoy then comes under attack and Shepard orders them to move out and leave the squad behind. After Shepard manages to fight through the ruins and back to the convoy, Eve proposes an idea to eliminate the Reaper. She mentions that the Shroud is near the two largest Maw Hammers in existence, and they can summon Kalros, "The Mother of all Thresher Maws". Eve says that Tuchanka is as much her home as it is the krogans', so if the hammers are activated, then she will come. While the maw has the Reaper distracted, the salarian scientist can finish the cure. As Shepard sets off, Eve heads into a nearby lab with her salarian doctor to finish the cure. If the Commander saved Maelon's data, then Eve survives the procedure to cure the genophage, and Shepard later gains strong support from the krogan clans. At the conclusion of the mission, Eve finally reveals her birth name to the Commander and says that they will always be friends. She later sends a message to Shepard, informing the Commander of the various krogan clans gathering in the Kelphic Valley, to whom she promises to speak to ensure that genophage cure isn't taken for granted. If Shepard chose to destroy Maelon's data back in 2185, however, Eve dies due to complications from having incomplete data, regardless of whether Shepard sabotaged the genophage cure or not. This causes several krogan clans to fall into conflict over who was responsible for Eve's death, weakening them as a whole. The krogan hold a funeral for her, attended by many krogan, the Urdnot leader, as well as Shepard. Her body is brought to the center of the Hollows, incinerated in a funeral pyre. Eve's eulogy is given by the current Urdnot shaman. Even if the genophage is dealt with, Eve may still die later, if Shepard does not aid Lieutenant Victus in disarming a rearmed turian bomb left over from the Krogan Rebellions. Eve was rallying the clans in the Kelphic Valley when the bomb explodes, obliterating her and the krogan population present. Shepard shortly receives a message from the Urdnot leader stating she died.

This page is a walkthrough of Mass Effect 3's mission structure, dividing plot progression into a Prologue and three Acts, each Priority mission gating the next. The Prologue covers Prologue: Earth (escaping the Reaper invasion aboard the Normandy SR-2), Priority: Mars (saving Liara T'Soni and retrieving Crucible data), and Priority: The Citadel I (rallying the galaxy's races). Act I runs Priority: Palaven (rescuing the turian primarch), Priority: Sur'Kesh (a war summit of turian, salarian, and krogan leaders, then protecting a krogan female from Cerberus), and Priority: Tuchanka (escorting the krogan female and a salarian scientist to the Shroud to disperse a genophage cure). Act II covers Priority: The Citadel II (stopping a Cerberus coup against the Council), Perseus Veil, Geth Dreadnought, Rannoch (deactivating the Reaper signal upgrading the geth), The Citadel III, Thessia (retrieving Catalyst information as the Reapers devastate the planet), and Horizon. Act III is Priority: Cerberus Headquarters (recapturing a Prothean VI that can identify the Catalyst) and Priority: Earth (the final battle and Crucible deployment).

The page then lists side missions grouped by the Priority mission that unlocks them, flagging "progress-sensitive" missions that expire when a later plot mission is completed and "timed" missions marked failed after a set number of missions (for example Tuchanka: Bomb, within three missions). It warns that no side missions can be done once Priority: Cerberus Headquarters begins. It notes DLC missions folded into progression (Priority: Eden Prime from From Ashes, Citadel: Aria T'Loak from Omega, Citadel: Dr. Bryson from Leviathan, Citadel: Shore Leave from Citadel) and Mass Effect 2 squadmate cameos in specific side missions: Kasumi Goto in Citadel: Hanar Diplomat, Jack in Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation, Grunt in Attican Traverse: Krogan Team, Jacob Taylor in Arrae: Ex-Cerberus Scientists, Zaeed Massani in Citadel: Volus Ambassador, and Samara in Kallini: Ardat-Yakshi Monastery. Attican Traverse: Krogan Team and Tuchanka: Turian Platoon each unlock Priority: Tuchanka, and Rannoch: Admiral Koris and Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons unlock Priority: Rannoch. It notes Legendary Edition includes all former DLC while keeping prerequisites largely intact.

The Krogan Rebellions were a major war between the krogan and the Citadel Council that began in 700 CE and lasted decades, preceded by over three centuries of aggressive krogan expansion and booming population growth. In gratitude for krogan service in the Rachni Wars, the Council had given them the conquered rachni worlds and several pristine habitable planets, but the krogan's high birth rate and lack of predators let them spread "like a plague" and annex territory from other Citadel races. When the krogan tried to settle the asari colony Lusia and refused Council demands to leave, their representative Overlord Kredak stormed out of the Council chambers daring them to take the worlds back, and war broke out.

The Council had pre-drafted STG operators and asari huntresses into the Office of Special Tactics and Reconnaissance, and the Spectres opened the war with crippling strikes: extranet viruses, sabotaged antimatter refineries, and headquarters stations rammed by pre-placed suicide freighters. But the krogan replenished losses easily and victory seemed inevitable, so the Council turned to the newly arrived turians, who established hidden command centers such as Pinnacle Station. The krogan retaliated by using asteroids to render three turian worlds uninhabitable, which only hardened turian resolve, since turian doctrine was to stop an enemy from ever becoming a threat again. The turians obtained the salarian-engineered genophage, intended by the salarians only as a deterrent, and deployed it in 710 CE, cutting successful krogan births to one in a thousand. The fertile female warlord Shiagur drew the strongest males to her band but was killed by turian peacekeepers at the Battle of Canrum, the last krogan push; vengeful krogan later hunted down the turians responsible. Besieged on all sides, the krogan surrendered, though rogue warlords fought on or became pirates. The turians were rewarded with a Council seat. The krogan remained deeply bitter, as Wrex put it, "to thank us for wiping out the rachni they neutered us all." A movement to remove the Krogan Monument failed. In 2185 a mass grave of about 430 turian soldiers from the Rebellions was uncovered on Uresium and repatriated to Palaven.

evidence.text: Garrus and Joker in the Cockpit. 2186, after Tuchanka the cockpit and the main battery, Normandy SR-2 He admits reservations: he doubts he could have gone along with the alliance if it had not been Palaven that needed krogan help, and he imagines the carnage if some hothead takes over from Wrex. His joke is about hiring Wrex a food taster.

Kaidan Cooks a Canadian Meal. 2186, Citadel shore leave, after the Cerberus coup on the Citadel Apollo's Cafe in the Presidium Commons, then Shepard's personal apartment on the Silversun Strip Shepard invites Kaidan up to the personal apartment. He arrives insisting on cooking "beef, bacon and beer, the food of my people," and splits a bottle with Shepard before he starts. He gets distracted, burns the garlic, and Shepard suggests hot sauce.

I'm a food inspector."* - *Guard: "Uh...I'm going to need to see some credentials."* - *Wrex: "You don't need to call for backup. I'm just looking for a game that isn't crap."* - *Guard: "We, uh, like to be prepared, sir."* - *Wrex: "Hey, you call that guarding?"* - *Guard: "Is there a problem you'd like to report, sir?"* - When it is revealed that Elijah Khan is already dead, Wrex is annoyed he got dressed in his ridiculous outfit but did not get to do the shooting. Good times." - If Wrex shoots Brooks, the krogan remarks that Shepard is "getting slow."

#### Mass Effect |  | Audio: Normandy SR\-1 | | --- | --- | The Normandy is a prototype starship, developed by the human Systems Alliance with the assistance of the Citadel Council. It is optimized for scouting and reconnaissance missions in unstable regions, using state\-of\-the\-art stealth technology. For most ships, the heat generated through standard operations is easily detectable against the absolute\-zero background of space. The Normandy, however, is able to temporarily sink this heat within the hull. Combined with refrigeration of the exterior hull, the ship can travel undetected for hours, or drift passively for days of covert observation. This is not without risk. The stored heat must eventually be radiated, or it will build to levels capable of cooking the crew alive. Another component of the stealth system is the Normandy’s revolutionary Tantalus drive, a mass effect core twice the standard size. The Tantalus drive generates mass concentrations that the Normandy 'falls into', allowing it to move without the use of heat\-emitting thrusters. #### Mass Effect 2 |  | Audio: Normandy SR\-1 | | --- | --- | The Systems Alliance Space Vehicle Normandy is a prototype starship created as a joint human and turian venture. A frigate optimized for reconnaissance missions, the vessel uses state\-of\-the\-art stealth technology. Most ships generate tremendous heat that is easily detectable against the absolute\-zero background of space. The Normandy, however, temporarily sinks this heat within its hull. Because of exterior hull refrigeration, the ship can travel undetected for hours, or drift passively for days of covert observation. That heat\-sinking carries the risk of cooking the crew alive if the stored heat is not eventually radiated. Also contributing to stealth is the Normandy's revolutionary Tantalus drive, a mass effect core double the standard size. The Tantalus generates mass concentrations that the Normandy "falls into," allowing it to move without the use of heat\-emitting thrusters.

This page collects the squad barks, conversation lines, and spontaneous remarks Urdnot Wrex delivers when he is in Commander Shepard's squad, drawn from Mass Effect and Mass Effect 3 (including the Citadel DLC). The lines showcase his bluntness, love of violence, contempt for turians and salarians, and pride in fallen krogan glory. Representative quotes:

Wrex, when Shepard spares the warehouse workers during Citadel: Expose Saren: "It would've been quicker to just to kill them."

Wrex, to Executor Pallin claiming he never bends the law: "Don't piss in my ear and tell me it's raining, I've known plenty of dirty C-Sec agents."

Wrex, meeting the Thorian on Feros: "And they call *me* ugly..."

Wrex, opening negotiations with the Rachni Queen at Peak 15: "This is going to be a fun conversation."

Wrex, to the Mira VI when it insists neutron radiation is lethal to all known life: "I won't have some virtual wench questioning my fitness!"

Wrex, if brought without Garrus on Garrus: Find Dr. Saleon: "If you're too weak to hunt, you don't deserve the kill."

Wrex, at the Krogan Monument on the Presidium: "This statue represents what the krogan use to be: a proud and fierce nation. Now we're just brutes for hire to the highest bidder. We've forgotten our roots."

Wrex, to Tali at the Krogan Monument: "At least you still live. In another two hundred years, this statue may be the only evidence my people ever existed."

Wrex, on Therum's surface: "Fifty degrees hotter and I might start to feel uncomfortable. How are you mammals doing, Shepard?"

Wrex, on Ilos: "There's something in the air here; death is on the wind. It's a good place for killing."

Wrex, distracting a guard during Silver Coast Casino: Infiltration: "I need to look at your kitchen. I'm a food inspector."

Wrex, after the squad guns down Shepard's pursuers in Citadel Archives: Escape: "That's why I love hanging out with you guys! Why shoot something once when you can shoot it 46 more times?"

Wrex, trapped in the vault with Shepard: "Refresh my memory. Didn't we used to win these things back in the old days?"

Wrex, in combat during Mass Effect 3: "Uncle Urdnot has a present for you!"

Wrex, if Shepard talks Brooks into surrender during Retake the Normandy: "In the old days, we would have just shot her. Good times."

The page also notes recurring bits: Wrex and Garrus argue in Citadel elevators about the genophage and about whether Shepard or Saren would win a fight, and Wrex repeatedly disdains bars that want to hire krogan bouncers "as a status symbol."

Ever jocular if he was pals with Shepard way back, he still manages to remark that he likes what Shepard has done to the Normandy, and depending on Shepard's relationship with Liara, attributes his "lack of windows" to his ability (or lack thereof) to kiss. According to Wrex, he hopes the food on the Normandy has gotten better since the days of chasing Saren across the galaxy. Aboard the Normandy, Wrex hears of news from his contacts regarding krogan problems better discussed "somewhere else" while Primarch Victus also wants to discuss some turian problems "in private". Shepard hears both out, and Wrex reveals that some of his scouts have gone missing while investigating suspicious activity in former rachni territory. If Shepard follows through with investigating the scouts before dealing with the genophage, Wrex feels miffed on missing a hell of a fight, restless that he's stuck talking and keeping the peace while there's a war going on. Wrex approves of the rachni queen dying and disapproves of cutting a deal with it, telling Shepard that if the rachni get out of line again the consequences are on the Commander's head. In a similar vein, he approves of Grunt surviving his last stand, and regrets losing Urdnot Dagg (or Grunt if he wasn't loyal to Shepard). If Shepard puts off investigating the scouts' disappearance though, Wrex simply mails Shepard what he thinks since he's no longer in the Normandy at the time. Victus' turian problems are of import to Wrex since the knowledge may kill any possible hope of an alliance. If Shepard takes care of the situation before dealing with the genophage, Wrex learns there and then that the ancient turians actually planted a bomb on krogan soil, nearly exploding when Cerberus tampered with it. Wrex personally gives Victus an earful on the Normandy, unmindful of the sacrifice the latter's son took to disable the bomb. Wrex's attitude towards Shepard after this is still shaped by the cumulative events, raising or lowering depending on the Commander's actions and attitudes in the past. If Shepard chooses to deal with this particular problem after the genophage Wrex never gets the opportunity to glower at the Primarch. Eventually the salarian doc proclaims Eve ready for travel to Tuchanka, to complete the last leg of the genophage cure on\-site. Shepard and company also learn that a Reaper Destroyer guards the site where the cure is supposed to be dispersed, the Shroud. Wrex is undeterred by the odds, his anticipation of curing the genophage fueling his drive and driving off any lingering discomfort from his "procedure". Shepard is then secretly contacted by the salarian dalatrass, who offers a deal: sabotage the cure and receive full salarian support, with the method of dealing with Wrex and the salarian doctor being the Commander's problem. Wrex orders the clans to assemble at the Hollows, riding with Shepard down to the planet. His brood brother Wreav radios in to say that Reapers have begun attacking the Hollows. Wrex orders Shepard to keep the Reapers away from Eve while he sorts out what's happening with the other clans, reemerging later bloodied but positively beaming. Wreav questions the presence of a salarian on krogan ground, and Wrex responds that the doctor is with him. Traditionalist Wreav doesn't buy Wrex's authority leading to a brief standoff, but Eve intervenes in the nick of time. She agitates the krogan present into fighting for their future, and Wrex is the first one to support her sentiments. The gathered clans set off in their tomkahs and make their way toward the Destroyer, intending to attack the Reaper on foot to divert its attention from the Shroud while Victus' turians provide air support. Inside a tomkah, Wrex rambles on his plans for the future, saying that for starters he'll demand the Council to return some of the old krogan territory as the krogan will need room to expand and recapture the glory of the ancients. Additionally he wants a new homeworld (or ten) on the basis that he'll not have his children suffocate in Tuchanka's harsh environs, wanting them to witness a resurgent krogan empire. He has enough decency to ask the Council for permission first, and while Eve and the salarian doctor temper his opinions with their own, Shepard lapses back to dalatrass Linron's deal. Shepard can inform Wrex and the others of the dalatrass' insidious offer. In the first attempt during the shuttle ride down the confession is cut off by turbulence, but if Shepard persists the truth becomes known. Wrex's trust in Shepard is reinforced if the Commander previously saved Maelon's cure, accepting Shepard's prior apology if the Commander regrets destroying the cure, and has trouble understanding Shepard's actions if Shepard was previously unrepentant.
