**Prerequisite:** Citadel: Expose Saren The assignment can be acquired in two ways. First, Urdnot Wrex must have been recruited. Aboard the SSV Normandy, repeatedly approaching Wrex and conversing with him about his past will eventually unlock an option to talk about his family, where he tells Shepard about the armor. Alternatively, this assignment can be acquired by visiting Tuntau (Phoenix system, Argos Rho), at the place labeled Hidden Structure on the map, after taking command of the Normandy.

Kaidan's presence during Shepard's shore leave adventures and beyond is contingent on him not being dead or sent to Admiral Hackett after the failed Citadel coup. If Kaidan is romanced, he will be the first one to come to Shepard's aid during the ambush in the Wards. Otherwise he will arrive at the apartment with the rest of the squad. After the conclusion of Shepard's clone fiasco, Kaidan can serve as back\-up for the Commander during matches in the Armax Arsenal Arena. Shepard can also invite Kaidan up to their Personal Apartment. When he arrives, he insists on cooking a Canadian meal of "beef, bacon and beer, the food of \[his] people" for Shepard, guzzling a bottle with his Commander before starting. If Shepard and Kaidan are lovers, the couple ask each other about their culinary skills. Shepard can either claim a roommate at Arcturus Station taught them to cook or claim expertise given time to practice, and Kaidan reveals that he learned to cook during his training with Conatix. Kaidan is distracted enough to burn the garlic on his recipe, and Shepard helpfully suggests hot sauce. After dinner the couple either can cuddle on the couch or go upstairs to "burn off" their calories. If Kaidan and Shepard's relationship is platonic, Shepard verbally trashes Kaidan's cooking, playfully wary of any "food poisoning". The Commander either "threatens" to put him on kitchen detail with Adams for a month, or emphasizes how the close calls they had over the years is apparently nothing compared to Kaidan's cooking. Kaidan just shakes his head and responds with indignation. After the dinner Shepard can admit approval at the meal, in which case Kaidan conflates his kitchen skills with winning a fight with James, or continue bantering with Kaidan in a friendly manner, accusing each other of being too "sensitive." Despite being on Shepard's team, Kaidan is an optional invite to the Commander's big party. During the first part of a loud party, he can be found with James and Steve. If Jack is present, Kaidan will remind her to keep her biotics under control. If she is not present, Kaidan will be the one to answer the question of what happens when a biotic gets drunk, saying it's just like everyone else except he glows blue when he does it. Steve will tease Kaidan about being a cheap date and asks about biotic party tricks, which Kaidan says are much more impressive when the audience is also drunk. Kaidan can be found in the same place in the first stage of a quiet party, agreeing with Jack about not trusting Cerberus, and suggesting that the party get a bit crazier. If Wrex is present but Jack is not, he and Kaidan will reminisce about Ashley. During the second stage of an energetic party, he can be found with Liara and James in their argument about biotic versus physical superiority. When James makes a jab about "flawed implants" Kaidan will shoot back with how hard he's worked and his resulting ability to Reave, to Liara and possibly Jacob's consternation. If Shepard sides with physical superiority , Kaidan will be flabbergasted, prompting Shepard to comfort him by saying that Kaidan's kind of physical excellence is still Shepard's kind of physical excellence. Kaidan will eventually confirm for James that as a child he frequently threw things around with his biotics. During the second stage of a quiet party, he can be found with Joker and Samantha on the second floor. While they are discussing EDI, Kaidan will bring up the time her body almost killed him. Later, Joker will ask the long burning question of how Kaidan gets his hair to stand up like that; it's static buildup from his implants. During the last stage of a loud party, Kaidan can still be found on the balcony. If Shepard sided with biotics in the earlier argument, Kaidan will request a turn demonstrating biotic superiority on James. If Shepard sided with physical ability previously, he will be winning against James in a pushup contest with Liara rooting for him. In both cases, that group will then start dancing afterward. In the last stage of a quiet party, if Shepard chose preparing food in an earlier argument between EDI and Steve, Kaidan will be found in the kitchen with EDI and Samantha. At first he will be arguing with EDI about the amount of curry that should be used, and ends up offending Samantha when asking her help to make his point. When the group discusses the team dynamics of a party, EDI rules out Kaidan as the mingling specialist due to an occasional tendency to be judgmental.

Tonn Actus was a turian pirate and profiteer who specialized in collecting krogan armor and artifacts, especially items from the Krogan Rebellions. Urdnot Wrex hated him because Wrex's family armor, handed down for generations, was part of Actus' collection.

Wrex had intended to hunt Actus through the Argos Rho cluster to recover the armor and kill the pirate personally, but Actus kept several scattered bases and Wrex's travels with Commander Shepard delayed the search. Wrex's best lead placed Actus on the planet Tuntau in the Phoenix system. Shepard could travel to Tuntau and raid Actus' hidden base; Actus was killed in the resulting firefight, letting Wrex reclaim his armor. In combat Actus carried an assault rifle and a shotgun, used Immunity, Shield Boost, and Carnage, and began the fight positioned on a top balcony near a fuel tank whose detonation could kill him quickly. It was possible to raid the base and kill him without Wrex present or without ever formally taking up the assignment, and still recover the armor and discuss it with Wrex afterward aboard the Normandy.

The Urdnot Camp was a small, rubble-strewn settlement on the krogan homeworld of Tuchanka, controlled by Clan Urdnot. A shuttle landing pad connected to the camp proper by a derelict passageway. The camp contained the throne dais of Clan Urdnot's leader, a building housing the Urdnot shaman where representatives of other clans gathered, a varren-fighting pit, the clan's food stores (frequently raided by invasive pyjak), a merchant's kiosk run by Ratch, and the laboratory of the clan's Lord High Researcher, Fortack.

In 2185 Commander Shepard traveled to the Urdnot Camp to aid Mordin Solus in searching for a missing fellow Special Tasks Group member during the mission "Mordin: Old Blood," and to help Grunt complete his Rite of Passage in "Grunt: Rite of Passage." Shepard could also speak with the leader of Clan Urdnot, who was either Urdnot Wrex (if he survived Virmire and joined Shepard) or Urdnot Wreav. Additional activities included helping a krogan mechanic find a combustion manifold to repair a vehicle, addressing the clan's chronic pyjak infestation, and betting on a varren fight. If Urdnot Wrex was alive, a Clan Nakmor representative was present at the camp to negotiate an alliance with Clan Urdnot, and Shepard could interact with the negotiation. The traditionalist Gatatog Uvenk was also present, opposing the current clan leadership. Missions and assignments tied to the location included "Tuchanka: Urdnot Wrex," "Tuchanka: Combustion Manifold," "Tuchanka: Killing Pyjaks," and "Tuchanka: Old Blood: Missing Scout."

Normandy: Special Ingredients was a short Mass Effect 2 assignment. After the mission Freedom's Progress, Shepard could speak to Mess Sergeant Gardner on the crew deck of the Normandy SR-2 and ask whether he needed anything. Gardner explained he wanted better ingredients to improve the crew's meals before the suicide mission, and that most of the supplies were available at the Citadel. Shepard traveled to Level 27 of the Citadel, visited the Zakera Cafe store, and purchased the High-Grade Provision for 500 credits, then returned it to Gardner to complete the assignment. The reward was 40 experience. Completing it caused crew members such as Crewman Goldstein to later remark on the improved food quality.

**Canrum** is a small, rocky world with a trace atmosphere of methane and krypton. Its surface is mainly composed of magnesium and silicates with deposits of carbon. Canrum was the site of the warlord Shiagur's defeat by turian peacekeeping forces during the Krogan Rebellions. While this band was not especially powerful, Shiagur was a female warlord – and one of the few remaining fertile females, at that. She had, through viciousness and cunning, parlayed her unique value into a position of power. Krogan males competed for the right to join her band and lie with her. When Shiagur's death was announced, vengeful male krogan admirers near and far swore blood oaths against the participating turian crews. In the end, several thousand of the turian participants were killed in open combat or through assassination. To this day, many krogan proudly proclaim that they have the "blood of Shiagur."

Mass Effect 3: Reckoning was a free DLC pack for Mass Effect 3's multiplayer mode, announced February 21, 2013 and released February 26, 2013 worldwide for Xbox 360 and PC and for PlayStation 3 (February 27 in Europe). It was the last multiplayer DLC for Mass Effect 3. It added six multiplayer characters (Geth Juggernaut Soldier, Cabal Vanguard, Talon Mercenary Engineer, Krogan Warlord Sentinel, Alliance Infiltration Unit Infiltrator, Awakened Collector Adept); seven weapons (M-7 Lancer, M-11 Suppressor, Adas Anti-Synthetic Rifle, Blood Pack Punisher, Executioner Pistol, Geth Spitfire, Venom Shotgun); five weapon mods including Assault Rifle Ultralight Materials and pistol/SMG Power Magnifier; and two Gear upgrades, the Batarian Gauntlet and the Geth Scanner. The Krogan Warlord wielded a Biotic Hammer.

This Shadow Broker dossier, unlocked after the Lair of the Shadow Broker mission, covered Grunt, the vat-bred "prototype" krogan created by the warlord Okeer. The Broker assessed him as a minimal threat to the continuation of the genophage but recommended leaking knowledge of the "perfect krogan" and his location to the Salarian Special Tasks Group.

The dossier consists mainly of intercepted extranet and terminal activity showing Grunt teaching himself about his heritage and about warrior cultures. His krogan-history searches (krogan history, great wars, the genophage, Okeer, Tuchanka, Urdnot Wrex) repeatedly show terms erased or modified, as do searches that drift toward "large predators," "earth lizard wrex" and "dinosaurs." His human-history activity includes downloads of documentary and news footage on major military figures and awards, and then a turn to literature: he searches for "homer kipling hemmingway" and downloads works by Ernest Hemingway, completing the audiobooks of For Whom the Bell Tolls and The Old Man and the Sea (100%), abandoning The Sun Also Rises at 14%, and deleting A Farewell to Arms, before searching "sharks."

A transactions log records purchases from an "Ultra Black Ops Mega Catalog" including case lots of engine oil, boxes of Fishdog Food Factory "Tastee Bites" and Batax's Hot Fish Spice, and video downloads: an unauthorized biography of Warlord Okeer, When Fauna Attacks! Volumes 1-10, Vaenia, Asari Confessions 26: True Blue, a Fornax "Krogan Edition" spotlight, and a "Garr the Krogan Battlemaster" action figure "with real smash your enemies action."

Canrum was the fourth planet of the Hydra System in the Argos Rho cluster, a small, rocky world with a trace atmosphere of methane and krypton. Its surface was composed mainly of magnesium and silicates with deposits of carbon.

Canrum was the site of the warlord Shiagur's defeat by turian peacekeeping forces during the Krogan Rebellions. Shiagur's band was not especially powerful, but she was a female warlord and one of the few remaining fertile females. Through viciousness and cunning she had turned her unique value into a position of power, with krogan males competing for the right to join her band and lie with her. When her death was announced, vengeful male krogan admirers near and far swore blood oaths against the turian crews that had participated. Ultimately several thousand of those turians were killed in open combat or by assassination, and to this day many krogan proudly claim to carry the "blood of Shiagur."

In Mass Effect 3, scans of Canrum revealed dangerous radiation coming from orbit. Chief Engineer Adams conducted further scans and discovered the remains of an ancient warhead marked with the Parthia Colony insignia, tied to the collection assignment UNC: Turian Insignias. The planet also featured a Haptic Optics Array as part of Search and Rescue. Canrum was referred to as "Sywinlon" in the first game's internal data. In Mass Effect 2 the krogan Grunt described the battle fought at Canrum as the last great battle of the Krogan Rebellions, dating it to the latter half of the 8th century CE.

"Dossier: The Warlord" was a Mass Effect 2 recruitment mission, available after Freedom's Progress as part of the Illusive Man's first set of dossiers. Dr. Okeer was described as a brilliant, brutal krogan warlord who had fought in the Krogan Rebellions, become obsessed with saving the krogan from the genophage, and was believed to have contacted the Collectors for technology to that end. He was operating from a Blue Suns camp on Korlus commanded by Jedore.

Fighting through Blue Suns forces (Troopers, Legionnaires, Centurions, and rocket-firing Heavies), Shepard's squad encountered a "Tank-Grown Krogan," only seven days old, one of Okeer's many rejected creations. He opened a path into the research base but would not accompany the squad. Inside, if Shepard had spared Rana Thanoptis on Virmire, she appeared and fled, saying she knew how Shepard worked. Okeer revealed he had been mass-producing and flash-indoctrinating tank-bred krogan in search of the "perfect" specimen, supplying his rejects as an army for Jedore, who could not command them. He wanted to bargain his knowledge of the Collectors for escape. Jedore then announced over the PA that Okeer had released the krogan without authorization and began pumping krogan-killing gas into the facility. Okeer chose to stay behind to protect his legacy, the perfect krogan in his tank.

Shepard fought Jedore, who wielded a rocket launcher and a YMIR Mech while tank-bred krogan broke loose around her, and killed her. Returning to the lab, Shepard found Okeer already dead from the toxins; his final recorded words asked Shepard to protect his legacy and admitted he had not known what the Collectors planned for the human colonists. The tank was recovered to the Normandy. Opening it (in the separate mission "Dr. Okeer's Legacy") released Grunt, who slammed Shepard against a wall before being persuaded or forced to back down; impressed by Shepard's strength, he joined the crew. Rewards included platinum and Sniper Rifle Damage and Krogan Vitality upgrades. If Grunt was never released he would not appear in Mass Effect 3; if released and surviving the suicide mission, he later led a krogan commando unit investigating a resurgent rachni. The mission was written by Lukas Kristjanson after a first pass by Brian Kindregan.

|  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | The **Shroud** is a salarian construct on the surface of Tuchanka. It was originally built to stabilize the atmosphere of Tuchanka due to the self\-induced nuclear winter of the krogan. The Shroud was deployed through the use of a number of ground\-based towers, which acted as mass\-drivers that launched the Shroud's components into orbit. Later, all but one of these towers were destroyed; this remaining tower became known as the Shroud, although the label is technically incorrect. The Shroud tower was repurposed to disperse particles and chemicals into Tuchanka's atmosphere, primarily for climate\-control purposes. After the Krogan Rebellions, the Shroud was sabotaged by an STG team to prevent any potential cure for the genophage from being disseminated through it.

To complete the treaty between the krogan and the turians, the Clan Urdnot leader (Wrex / Wreav) insists that the genophage must be cured. Mordin Solus / Padok Wiks needs time to stabilize Eve and prepare the cure — **at minimum, either Tuchanka: Turian Platoon OR Attican Traverse: Krogan Team must be finished** before Eve is declared ready for transport to Tuchanka. This is a good time to finish the time\-sensitive missions mentioned above. The genophage cure is to be dispersed from the top of the Shroud, a tower constructed by the salarians to stabilize the atmosphere of Tuchanka, and later covertly used by the turians to disperse the original genophage virus. The salarian STG member that prepared the cure will travel to the Shroud with Eve and ensure that this takes place. Travel to the planet Tuchanka in the Krogan DMZ and select the proper NavPoint. In the cutscene, you discover that the Reapers are using the Shroud to poison Tuchanka's atmosphere. It is impossible to land the shuttle at the Shroud site due to the presence of a Reaper Destroyer there. It is decided that the krogan will attack the Reaper from the ground while turian fighters fly air support. The salarian Dalatrass then privately contacts Shepard and reveals that the Shroud was sabotaged to prevent dispersal of a cure. She suggests tricking the krogan into thinking that the cure has been deployed, and offers salarian support for the war effort if Shepard does so.

**Prerequisite:** Priority: Sur'Kesh **Prerequisite:** Attican Traverse: Krogan Team or Tuchanka: Turian Platoon This mission is automatically acquired after Eve's retrieval from Sur'Kesh. However, actually finishing this mission requires completing *either* mission given by the turian and krogan leaders aboard the Normandy. The journal text updates to the following entry upon fulfillment of the condition: *“The genophage cure is a success, but it must be synthesized and dispersed across all of Tuchanka using the Shroud tower. Land on Tuchanka and get Eve safely to the tower.”* The NavPoint for this mission is now available on Tuchanka. Upon landing on the planet, the final journal update is shown: *“The plan to disperse the genophage cure has been complicated by the arrival of Reaper forces, who have occupied the area near the shroud tower. Get Eve safely to the tower.”*

The Shroud was a salarian construct on the surface of Tuchanka, built roughly 2,000 years ago to stabilize the planet's atmosphere after the krogan's self-induced nuclear winter. It was originally deployed by a series of ground-based mass-driver towers that launched its components into orbit; all but one of those towers were later destroyed, and that surviving tower came to be called "the Shroud," though the name was technically inaccurate. The tower was repurposed to disperse particles and chemicals into Tuchanka's atmosphere for climate control.

The Shroud was part of a salarian scheme to uplift the krogan during the Rachni Wars, when a losing Council traded technology to the krogan in exchange for soldiers. During the subsequent Krogan Rebellions, after the genophage was released, a salarian STG team sabotaged the Shroud to ensure that any genophage cure could not be easily disseminated through it. The structure stood in an old arena built as a shrine to Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws, placed there in the hope that the threat would deter anyone from reaching the Shroud and discovering the sabotage.

In Mass Effect 3, Commander Shepard and Mordin Solus (or Padok Wiks) needed the Shroud to disperse a genophage cure across Tuchanka as part of securing a turian-krogan alliance. A Destroyer-class Reaper had seized the tower to poison the atmosphere. Shepard's squad dodged its beam to reach two maw hammers that summoned Kalros, who attacked the Destroyer; the Reaper smashed her into the Shroud, damaging it, but Kalros dragged the Reaper underground. Shepard then reached the control room, where a temperature malfunction and the STG countermeasures made remote bypass impossible, forcing the salarian scientist to access the controls manually. Whether or not the cure was distributed, the Shroud was ultimately destroyed in an explosion.

The krogan head out in a convoy towards the Shroud. While travelling, you're given the option again to reveal the Dalatrass's deal or keep quiet about it. Soon after, the convoy comes to an immediate halt, and the team dismounts to find out why. Running around is recommended, as the area is a treasure trove of loot. You can pick up a Shotgun Smart Choke upgrade, a Death Mask helmet, a Pistol Melee Stunner, a Pistol Magazine Upgrade, the Graal Spike Thrower shotgun, and 2 Med\-kits around. A couple of krogan interactions are optional: you can speak to one fixing and complaining about a tomkah's combustion manifold, and there's another who was the owner of the Graal you took and wants whatever you kill with it as his "trophies". To kick off the next part of the plot, however, speak to the Krogan Scout, who tells you that the road is damaged and the convoy can't proceed further. However, the turian air support has already begun their attack, and are too close to call it off. A fighter is shot down by the Reaper and hits a truck. Shepard radios the Urdnot leader to get out of the area. However, you and the squad are left behind and have to find an alternative route. At this point, you gain another 150 experience. The only path left is through the ruins. Jump over a gap and head into the tunnel.

With all opposition from the Reapers destroyed, Shepard and the salarian doctor approach the Shroud, their associates having been told to retreat to safety. However, the Shroud sustained damage in the fight against the Reaper – it is falling to pieces as Shepard approaches. Within, Eve's STG caretaker – Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks – is attempting to stabilize the structure. He will also report on Eve's status; in the absence of Maelon's data, she will have died whilst Shepard handled the Reaper. All outcomes are available regardless of whether Mordin or Wiks is present, so for convenience we will refer to the character as "Mordin". At this point, Shepard may either let Mordin go or stop him to sabotage the cure per the Dalatrass's request. There are multiple outcomes to this conversation: - If Shepard warned of the Dalatrass's deal in the convoy, Mordin deploys the counter\-sabotage and deploys the cure, sacrificing his life in the process. This is the only outcome in this situation. You may use a Paragon interrupt just before Mordin steps into the elevator to get some morality points, but it won't change Mordin's fate. - If Shepard did not reveal the sabotage while in the convoy to the Shroud, Mordin will realize something is wrong. Either Shepard tells Mordin about the Dalatrass's deal, or Mordin will correctly surmise it. If Shepard tries to sabotage the cure, and Wrex and/or Eve are alive, Mordin will refuse to listen. Shepard is offered a Renegade interrupt to gun him down. If Shepard does not take it, Mordin will deploy the counter\-sabotage and successfully cure the Genophage but die in the explosion that follows; otherwise, the sabotage is left intact, and the cure fails. - If Shepard has not revealed the sabotage and tries to make Mordin abandon the mission while Wrex and Eve are *both* dead, persuade options can be used on Mordin to convince him that it is for the best if the Shroud remain sabotaged and the krogan fooled into believing the genophage cured. This is the only scenario where Mordin lives. Both Mordin and Wiks agree to fake their own deaths, but Mordin becomes a War Asset at the Crucible project, whereas Wiks, according to an e\-mail he sends you after the mission, instead seeks out a quiet colony world where he will work as a farmer and take his secret to the grave.

- Priority: Palaven \- Rescue a turian primarch. - Priority: Sur'Kesh \- Hold a war summit with the turian, salarian, and krogan leaders, then protect a krogan female from a Cerberus attack. - Priority: Tuchanka \- Escort the krogan female and a salarian scientist to the Shroud to disperse a cure for the genophage.

What the krogan call the Shroud is a technological remnant of the Salarian Uplift. After Tuchanka's nuclear war released tons of smoke and dust into the atmosphere, the planet temporarily cooled from global dimming\-\-except at the poles, where the albedo was lowered by soot. As clouds trapped the resulting heat, enormous swaths of permafrost melted, releasing methane captured in clathrates from previous millennia. This potent greenhouse gas created a runaway heat cycle that was called "the nuclear summer." Without intervention, Tuchanka would have sunk into a slow but certain mass extinction. The salarian solution was to assemble the Shroud, a permanent sun shield of trillions of tiny diffractory lenses placed at the L1 Lagrange point, the point in space where the lenses' naturally stable orbit would shade the planet. The salarians settled on a delivery method that became known as the Shroud Towers. The towers were essentially enormous coilguns that could fire a payload of lenses into space along with the equipment necessary to monitor the payload's trajectories. Many krogan warlords enthusiastically approved of the plan, some because they believed in saving their homeworld, but most because they saw future military applications for the Shroud Towers. The Shroud was completed on schedule over the next few decades, by which time the rachni held the warlords' full attention. The Krogan Rebellions were not kind to the Shroud Towers. All but one was destroyed during the push for krogan demilitarization. The remaining tower, often referred to as "the Shroud" even though that is technically incorrect, was repurposed for cloud seeding and atmospheric repair. It remains on the landscape as an anachronism, a symbol of a time when krogan and salarians helped themselves by aiding one another.

codex.text: - Jorgal Thurak: krogan of Clan Jorgal and Blood Pack representative present at the Hollows on Tuchanka under Urdnot Wreav's leadership; he objected to the salarian scientist, drew weapons on Wreav, joined the anti-Reaper convoy, and was dragged underground and killed by the thresher maw Kalros. (source: Jorgal Thurak)

- Urdnot Wreav, Wrex's traditionalist broodbrother, became leader of Clan Urdnot if Wrex died on Virmire or never joined Shepard; he prized his clan over the krogan race, stockpiled more weapons of mass destruction than any krogan in history, claimed personal credit for curing the genophage, and could be duped into pledging krogan support if the salarian sabotage was concealed (source: Urdnot Wreav).

- Krogan traditionalists like Gatatog Uvenk championed the warrior culture that once threatened the Citadel races during the Krogan Rebellions, viewing Clan Urdnot's reforms under Wrex as weakening the krogan, while deferring instead to the more conservative Wreav; fear that his own clan would be reduced to bodies buried in Tuchanka's soil eventually drove Uvenk to seek an alliance with Urdnot. (source: Gatatog Uvenk)
- The Hollows serve as sacred neutral ground where all krogan clans can meet. (source: Urdnot Wreav)

- Clan Urdnot is a krogan tribe on Tuchanka that by 2186 became the uncontested representative of krogan power to the galaxy, having absorbed or wiped out Clans Nakmor, Jurdon, Quash, and Raik; it is led by Urdnot Wrex or his brother Urdnot Wreav depending on Shepard's actions in Mass Effect. (source: Clan Urdnot)

- Under Urdnot Wrex, Clan Urdnot became a reformist faction holding neutral ground open to all krogan and redirecting research from weapons to crop genetics and medicine; under Urdnot Wreav it remained an aggressive traditional clan that stockpiled weapons of mass destruction. (source: Clan Urdnot)
- Wreav is more traditional than Wrex and prioritizes the interests of Clan Urdnot over the krogan race as a whole. (source: Urdnot Wreav)

- Whether Wrex or Urdnot Wreav led the krogan into Mass Effect 3 determined the "Clan Urdnot" and "Krogan Mercenaries" War Assets and whether a sabotaged genophage cure could be concealed (source: Virmire: Wrex and the Genophage).
